title: Bwindi vs Volcanoes National Park: Trade a Cheaper Permit for a Longer Drive, or Pay for Speed
meta_title: Bwindi vs Volcanoes: Gorilla Permits, Treks and Travel
meta_description: Bwindi vs Volcanoes compared: permit prices, trek difficulty, travel time from Kigali or Entebbe and lodges, so you can pick the right gorilla park.
excerpt: Bwindi vs Volcanoes compared side by side: Uganda's cheaper permits and wider choice of gorilla families against Rwanda's short drive from Kigali, with costs, trek difficulty and a clear verdict.
content:
The Bwindi vs Volcanoes decision comes down to money against time. Uganda's Bwindi Impenetrable National Park charges US$800 for a gorilla permit, while Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park charges US$1,500 (both checked October 2026), but Volcanoes is about two and a half to three hours from Kigali and Bwindi usually takes a full day to reach.

In any Bwindi vs Volcanoes comparison, remember that both parks protect the same species, mountain gorillas, and both give you exactly one hour with a habituated family. So the real question is which trip fits your budget, your fitness and the days you have. Below we compare permits, total costs, trek difficulty, travel times, lodges and what else you can add, with a clear verdict for each type of traveller.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Quick Facts

  • Bwindi vs Volcanoes permits: Bwindi US$800 (US$600 in April, May and November); Volcanoes US$1,500 (checked October 2026)
  • Rwanda discount: 30% off between November and May if you also stay two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe
  • Gateways: Volcanoes: Kigali, about 2.5-3 hours by road. Bwindi: Kigali (4-5 hours to the southern sectors) or Entebbe (8-10 hours, or a 1-2 hour flight)
  • Bwindi vs Volcanoes altitude: Bwindi about 1,160-2,600 m; Volcanoes mostly 2,400-3,500 m
  • Group rules: Maximum eight visitors per family, one hour with the gorillas, minimum age 15 in both parks
  • Best months: June to September and December to February are driest in both; trekking runs all year

Bwindi vs Volcanoes National Park at a Glance

Bwindi vs Volcanoes National Park is a comparison between two neighbours on either side of the Uganda-Rwanda border. Bwindi is a large, low rainforest with many gorilla families; Volcanoes is a smaller, higher park on the slopes of the Virunga volcanoes with excellent road access.

Bwindi Impenetrable National Park covers about 321 km² of steep forest in southwest Uganda and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994. The 2018 census counted 459 mountain gorillas in the Bwindi-Sarambwe ecosystem, close to half of the 1,063 known worldwide. Volcanoes National Park covers about 160 km² and protects the Rwandan side of the Virunga Massif, which it shares with Uganda's Mgahinga and Congo's Virunga park.

Bwindi vs VolcanoesBwindi (Uganda)Volcanoes (Rwanda)
Gorilla permitUS$800; US$600 in April, May and NovemberUS$1,500; US$1,050 with the November-May discount
Habituated familiesRoughly 20 or more across four sectorsAbout 12
Nearest airportKigali or Entebbe, plus airstrips at Kihihi and KisoroKigali International

TerrainDense, steep rainforest valleysFarmland, bamboo and volcano slopes

Best forValue, longer Uganda safaris, repeat treksShort trips, comfort, tight schedules

Bwindi vs Volcanoes fees checked October 2026. Habituated family numbers change as groups split or merge, so treat them as a guide.

Which Is Cheaper for Gorilla Trekking, Bwindi or Volcanoes?

Bwindi is clearly cheaper in the Bwindi vs Volcanoes price comparison. A Uganda permit costs US$800 against Rwanda's US$1,500, so a couple saves about US$1,400 on permits alone. Rwanda narrows the gap from November to May, and Uganda widens it again in its April, May and November low-season months.

Uganda's permit and low-season rate

The Uganda Wildlife Authority sets the Bwindi gorilla permit at US$800 for foreign non-residents, with a reduced US$600 rate for treks in April, May and November, the wettest months (checked October 2026). Low-season permits reportedly cannot be rescheduled, so only take one if your dates are fixed. The gorilla habituation experience in Rushaga costs US$1,500 until 31 December 2026 and is listed at US$1,800 from 1 January 2027. You can check current tariffs on the Uganda Wildlife Authority website, and our Bwindi gorilla trekking guide covers how the permits and sectors work.

Rwanda's permit and the November to May discount

Rwanda charges US$1,500 per foreign visitor for a gorilla permit in Volcanoes National Park. The Rwanda Development Board offers 30% off between November and May if you combine the trek with two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe (or one night in each) plus a paid activity there, which brings the permit down to US$1,050. The conditions are set out on the RDB low-season discount page, and our Rwanda gorilla permit guide walks through booking.

What a Bwindi vs Volcanoes trip costs by budget

Permits are only part of the Bwindi vs Volcanoes bill. Transport, lodges and park extras push totals well above the permit price, especially for Bwindi from Entebbe, where the long drive or a domestic flight adds cost. The ranges below are our estimates per person sharing, for one gorilla trek, and exclude international flights and visas.

Trip styleBwindi from Kigali (3 days)Volcanoes from Kigali (2 days)
BudgetUS$1,700-2,200US$2,100-2,600
Mid-rangeUS$2,200-3,200US$2,600-3,600
LuxuryUS$3,500 and upUS$5,000 and up

Estimates only, built from the permit fees above and typical lodge rate bands; your quote depends on season, group size and lodge choice. The gap is widest at the luxury end, where Rwanda's top lodges near Volcanoes charge far more than Bwindi's best camps.

Where Will You Have More Choice of Gorilla Families?

Bwindi offers more choice. On family numbers the Bwindi vs Volcanoes gap is wide: Bwindi's roughly 20 or more habituated families are spread across four sectors, Buhoma, Ruhija, Rushaga and Nkuringo, while Volcanoes has about 12 families trekked from a single headquarters at Kinigi. With eight visitors per family per day, Bwindi simply has more permits to go round.

Photo by 2H Media on Unsplash

That extra supply matters in the busy months. Permits for June to September and around Christmas can sell out months ahead in both countries, but Bwindi more often has a family free somewhere for late planners. The catch is that your permit is tied to one sector, and the sectors are one to four hours apart by road, so your lodge has to match it.

Volcanoes is simpler to organise. Everyone meets at Kinigi for an early briefing, rangers assign groups by fitness, and you drive a short way to your family's trailhead. If you would rather not think about sectors at all, that simplicity is part of what Rwanda's higher price buys in any Bwindi vs Volcanoes calculation.

How Hard Is the Gorilla Trek in Each Park?

Bwindi vs Volcanoes treks are both moderate to strenuous, but for different reasons. Volcanoes is higher, so the thin air makes you breathe hard on the climb; Bwindi is lower but steeper and more tangled. In both, reaching the family can take from under an hour to four hours or more, and nobody can promise which you will get.

On the Rwandan side of the Bwindi vs Volcanoes comparison, treks in Volcanoes National Park begin in farmland and climb into bamboo and forest on the volcano slopes, mostly between about 2,400 and 3,500 metres. Paths are often clearer than in Bwindi, but they turn very muddy in the rains, and the altitude slows most people down.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

On the Ugandan side, Bwindi's name is a fair warning. Its ridges and valleys run between about 1,160 and 2,600 metres, and rangers sometimes have to cut a way through thick undergrowth. The lower altitude helps your lungs, while the slippery descents test your knees. Our article on how hard gorilla trekking really is covers fitness, porters and trek times in detail.

Is Bwindi vs Volcanoes different for less mobile travellers?

Either park can work for travellers with limited fitness if you ask for an easier family and hire a porter, usually a local guide who carries your bag and helps on steep sections. Rwanda's short drive from Kigali also means less fatigue before the trek. Tell us about any mobility concerns before booking so we can request a suitable family.

How Do You Get to Bwindi and Volcanoes National Park?

Volcanoes is the easier park to reach, and travel time is the biggest Bwindi vs Volcanoes difference after price. Kigali has good long-haul connections and the road to Kinigi takes about two and a half to three hours. Bwindi means a long drive from Kigali or Entebbe, or a domestic flight plus a road transfer.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Reaching Volcanoes from Kigali

Many travellers land in Kigali, drive to Musanze or Kinigi the same afternoon and trek the next morning. A same-day trip is possible with a pre-dawn start, which is how our 1 day gorilla trekking safari in Rwanda works, though an overnight near the park makes the day far less rushed.

Reaching Bwindi from Kigali or Entebbe

Kigali is often the quickest road gateway to Bwindi's southern sectors: Rushaga and Nkuringo are roughly four to five hours away via the Cyanika border. From Entebbe, the drive to Buhoma takes about eight to ten hours. Scheduled flights from Entebbe to Kihihi (for Buhoma and Ruhija) or Kisoro (for Rushaga and Nkuringo) take about one to two hours, followed by a road transfer of an hour or more.

Crossing from Rwanda into Uganda means a second visa unless you hold the East Africa Tourist Visa, which covers Uganda, Kenya and Rwanda. Our guide to the East Africa Tourist Visa explains when it saves money.

What Else Can You Add Around Each Park?

Uganda gives you more to add on the same trip, which often tips the Bwindi vs Volcanoes decision for first-time visitors to Africa. From Bwindi you can continue to Queen Elizabeth National Park for game drives, Kibale for chimpanzees or Lake Bunyonyi to relax. Rwanda's extras are closer together and easier to slot into a short trip.

Around Bwindi, popular additions include a Batwa cultural walk, forest nature walks for birding, and the gorilla habituation experience in Rushaga, a longer visit of about four hours with a family still being used to people. Our 4 day gorilla trekking safari to Bwindi pairs the trek with the Batwa experience and Lake Bunyonyi.

Photo by 2H Media on Unsplash

Around Volcanoes, the classic add-ons are golden monkey trekking in the bamboo zone, the hike to Dian Fossey's grave at the Karisoke site, and the day hike up Mount Bisoke to its crater lake. Further afield, Rwanda pairs well with Lake Kivu, Nyungwe for chimpanzees, and Akagera for big game, and the last two also unlock the permit discount.

Lodges in each park

Bwindi's lodges sit in or near each of the four sectors, from simple community-run guesthouses to upmarket forest lodges, so choose your lodge only after your permit sector is confirmed. Volcanoes lodges cluster around Kinigi and Musanze, and Rwanda has some of the most expensive gorilla lodges in Africa at the top end, alongside comfortable mid-range options.

Insider Tips

  • Book permits first: Secure the permit, then the lodge; in Bwindi the sector decides where you sleep
  • Use the calendars: Rwanda's discount runs November to May; Uganda's US$600 rate covers April, May and November only
  • Pick your gateway: Flying into Kigali often suits both parks, so you can trek in either or both on one trip
  • Hire a porter: It helps on steep slopes and supports families living beside the parks
  • Pack for mud: Waterproof boots, gardening gloves for nettles and a rain jacket; see our gorilla trekking packing list
  • Trek in both countries: Some travellers trek once in each country to compare forests; Kigali makes this practical

Bwindi vs Volcanoes: Which Park Suits Your Trip?

Choose Bwindi if value, choice and a longer safari matter most; choose Volcanoes if time and comfort matter most. Neither offers better gorillas. In the Bwindi vs Volcanoes choice, your budget, your days and whether you want savannah wildlife on the same trip should decide.

Choose Bwindi if

You are watching costs, want to trek twice, or are planning a full Uganda safari with chimpanzees and tree-climbing lions. Bwindi also suits travellers who want the longer habituation experience, which Rwanda does not offer, and families with teenagers who meet the minimum age of 15.

Choose Volcanoes if

You have two or three days, want to land and trek with little road time, or are adding gorillas to a business trip or a Kenya or Tanzania safari. Rwanda's smooth roads and simple logistics justify the higher permit for many people, and our guide to gorilla trekking in Rwanda shows how a short trip comes together.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Bwindi or Volcanoes better for gorilla trekking?

Neither park is better for the gorillas themselves: both protect wild mountain gorillas and both give you one hour with a habituated family. In the Bwindi vs Volcanoes choice, Bwindi wins on permit price and choice of families, while Volcanoes wins on easy access from Kigali and short trips. Pick by budget and time, not by the animals.

Which is cheaper, Bwindi or Volcanoes National Park?

Bwindi is much cheaper. A Uganda gorilla permit costs US$800 for foreign non-residents, or US$600 for treks in April, May and November, while Rwanda charges US$1,500 at Volcanoes National Park, or US$1,050 with the November to May discount for qualifying stays (all checked October 2026). Confirm current rates before booking.

Can I trek gorillas in Bwindi from Kigali?

Yes. Kigali is often the easiest gateway to Bwindi's southern sectors, Rushaga and Nkuringo, which are roughly four to five hours by road via the Cyanika border. You need a Uganda visa or the East Africa Tourist Visa, and most people spend at least two nights near the park rather than attempting a same-day return.

Is the trek harder in Bwindi or Volcanoes?

The trek is hard in different ways. Volcanoes National Park sits higher, with most treks between about 2,400 and 3,500 metres, so you feel the thin air. Bwindi is lower, at roughly 1,160 to 2,600 metres, but its steep, tangled valleys and off-trail sections can make a long day just as tiring. Porters help in both parks.

How many days do I need for Bwindi or Volcanoes?

Volcanoes National Park works as a day trip from Kigali, though two or three days is more relaxed. Bwindi needs at least three days from Kigali and four from Entebbe, because the drive is long. If you are comparing Bwindi vs Volcanoes on a tight schedule, Rwanda saves you a day or two of travel.

Final Thoughts

Bwindi vs Volcanoes is not a contest between better and worse gorillas: it is a trade between Uganda's lower permit price and wider choice, and Rwanda's speed and simplicity. Pay for time with Volcanoes, or spend time to save money and see more of Uganda with Bwindi.

Permits for the dry months go early in both countries, so settle the Bwindi vs Volcanoes question, then secure the permit before anything else.
